newsitem.title: ITALY: ALITALIA SEE KLM AS "ATTRACTIVE" PARTNER.
newsitem.headline: ALITALIA SEE KLM AS "ATTRACTIVE" PARTNER.

text.p: Dutch airline KLM is an attractive potential partner for Alitalia, but any link-up would have to be carefully considered, the Italian carrier's chairman said in an interview published on Thursday.
"KLM is a very attractive candidate, but marriage is an important thing and has to be carefully thought about," Domenico Cempella told L'Espresso magazine.

KLM last week confirmed it was in talks with Alitalia on a possible alliance but played down reports they were at an advanced stage. Alitalia said earlier this week it did not expect to make any announcement on partnerships this month.

Air France has also been named by government officials as a possible partner for Italy's loss-making airline, but Cempella hinted that synergies between the two groups might not be as solid as between KLM and Alitalia.
Alitalia aims to make Milan's Malpensa airport its main hub for central and north Italy.
"Malpensa will take traffic from Zurich, Frankfurt, Paris and other great European airports," Cempella said.
Air France's main hub is Paris.
Cempella said the main point of an alliance would be to expand the Italian flag carrier's reach.
"We have an international network which is too small," he said. "We are in many continents but none of them with considerable weight.
"The future partner should change our international network from how it is now, integrating and interconnecting our routes," he added. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
